prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how big is a cost rise in percent? A supplier will raise the unit cost of every product by a flat 1.50 euros. For every product, return product_id, unit_cost_eur and rise_pct (the 1.50-euro rise as a percentage of today's unit cost, such as 5 for a 5% rise), in that order. Use exactly these column names and do not round. Every product has a unit_cost_eur above 0. One row per product, every product included. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the calculated column on the percentage scale. A rise of 1.50 euros on a 30-euro product is 5%, so rise_pct should be 5 there.
The query works out the rise as a share of the cost, a small number such as 0.05. A percentage is the same amount 100 times larger.
starter_sql:
SELECT product_id, unit_cost_eur, 1.50 / unit_cost_eur AS rise_pct
FROM products
why_this_works: 1.50 / unit_cost_eur is the rise as a share of the cost; multiplied by 100, it is the same amount as a percentage.
